newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.
The German discount rate, the floor on interest rates, was left at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate, the ceiling on rates, at 4.50 percent.
The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also kept steady at a fixed rate of three percent.
All 10 economists surveyed by Reuters expected the Bundesbank to leave interest rates unchanged at the meeting.

Signs that the economy may be starting to recover hold little immediate threat of a change in interest rates, analysts said. They argue that while inflation remained low but unemployment was at record post-war highs, there was little chance for either a rate cut or a rate hike.
The Economics Ministry reported this morning that industrial production grew 1.9 percent in February from the month before after falling 1.5 percent month-on-month in January.
